cranial nerve examination: partial right oculomotor palsy with right adduction failure, mild vertical gaze limitation, mildly impaired convergence, and partial ptosis; pupils equally reactive
mental status / cognitive screen: normal
muscle tone examination: normal
limb strength (MRC) examination: normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
sensory examination (pinprick, vibration, proprioception): normal
coordination examination (limb and truncal): normal
posture and pull test: normal
fundoscopy: normal
nystagmus: direction and whether it changes with gaze: no nystagmus
smooth pursuit and saccades: normal
adduction in horizontal gaze (each eye): on left gaze the right eye fails to adduct, and the contralateral eye shows NO abducting nystagmus - unlike a classic INO
abducting nystagmus of the fellow eye: absent
vertical gaze and convergence: mild vertical limitation and mildly impaired convergence
skew deviation / alternating cover test: no vertical misalignment
ocular torsion and head tilt: none
subjective visual vertical: within normal limits
head impulse test: normal - no corrective saccade
pupil size and light reaction: pupils EQUALLY REACTIVE - pupil-sparing
ptosis / lid position: partial ptosis
limb and truncal ataxia: absent
gait and tandem walking: normal
hearing and tinnitus: normal
facial dysmorphism and general examination: unremarkable
Glasgow Coma Scale on arrival: normal / non-contributory
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Microvascular (ischemic) partial right oculomotor (third) nerve palsy

Alternatives:
1. Posterior communicating artery aneurysm with atypical pupil-sparing compression of the right third nerve
2. Small paramedian midbrain infarct involving the right third nerve fascicle
3. Inflammatory/demyelinating lesion of the right third nerve (e.g., Miller Fisher syndrome variant)
